title: The Independent Calculation is load-bearing in the interim settlement rules but never defined in the process definition
content:
A.2.4.1.2.1 says the process definition "specifies who performs the calculations and how funds are ultimately paid out," and it names two artifacts: the Initial Calculation by each Operational Executor Agent (A.2.4.1.2.1.1) and the Final Calculation by Core GovOps (A.2.4.1.2.1.2). Agreed, Disputed and Final Amounts are all defined against those two.

The interim measures then rely on a third. A.2.4.1.2.1.5.2 refers to "The Independent Calculation prepared by the Core Council Risk Advisor on behalf of the Core Council," says it "will be prepared normally," and makes its amounts the ones "treated as Agreed Amounts" for everything outside the narrow disputable scope. A.2.4.1.2.1.5.3 and A.2.4.1.2.1.5.4 do the same.

Nothing in the enclosing process defines this artifact — no preparer's duties, no deadline, no required contents, no dispute path against it. "Prepared normally" points at a norm the Atlas has not written down. Yet during the interim it is the most consequential document in the cycle: for most line items, its figures become binding without any Prime Agent having the five-day dispute right that attaches to an Initial Calculation.

The likely explanation is sequencing — an existing Risk Advisor practice was pressed into service and the process definition was written around the target state. The practical consequence is a gap in exactly the place the Atlas is otherwise careful: an independent check on the Executor's numbers is clearly desirable, and it currently has less specification than the artifact it checks. Worth tracking, since interim measures have a habit of outlasting their labels.
description: Three interim sections make the Core Council Risk Advisor's Independent Calculation the source of amounts deemed agreed, yet the main MSC process defines only the Initial and Final Calculations.
